messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: need help on parser/highlight
parts:
Hi knitters,

This morning I was notified (aka Ripley'ed) that the parser package
was removed from the CRAN repository, which means this package will no
longer be available until its problems have been fixed (right now it
cannot pass R CMD check). Sadly, our R Enthusiast (aka Romain) does
not seem to be as enthusiastic on R as before, which leads to the
orphaned packages parser and highlight.

http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/parser/
http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/highlight/

As you know, the syntax highlighting and code reformatting features in
knitr rely on these two packages, so I'm wondering if anybody can save
them from the orphaned world. I really do not know much about C and I
know nothing about Bison.

http://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/parser/
http://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/highlight/

Or do you have other approaches for syntax highlighting? I do not
think we need that sophisticated/precise approaches as in highlight.
We might be able to highlight R code well just based on regular
expressions/text analysis instead of semantic analysis. I think
highlight.js is a good example.

I was given 6 days to deal with these problems, then either knitr will
be removed from CRAN as well, or I remove the dependencies on
highlight and parser.

Thanks!

Regards,
Yihui

messages.author: 30b406a9189eeb25
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] need help on parser/highlight
parts:
Hi Yihui, list,

What sad news!  Is it just syntax highlighting in LaTeX that is at stake here?  
Markdown doesn't have highlighting, and seems the more flexible road to html
since we can highlight with our preferred scheme in CSS (I like solarized).  

I like Romain's LaTeX highlighting way more than the other Sweave approaches,
but it feels entirely wrong that syntax highlighting is something managed by knitr,
instead of LaTeX itself.  

I haven't explored this much, but is there a reason we can't just have LaTeX syntax
highlighting using a native package (e.g. minted, pygments, listings?)  Am I missing 
something here?

Carl

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] need help on parser/highlight
parts:
Romain's highlight is precise in terms of recognizing all R symbols.
Some LaTeX packages may highlight *weighted.mean*() as
weighted.*mean*() if the highlighting is keywords-based, and only a
limited number of keywords are provided in them. The other problem is
that they often involve with a number of dependencies, so I need an
extra instruction on how to install LaTeX packages. This may not be a
big deal. I'll take a look at the packages you mentioned in the link.
Thanks!

Actually highlight also supports highlighting in HTML. This is useful
for some people, e.g.
http://geospaced.blogspot.com/2012/05/knitr-cactus-twitterbootstrap-jquery.html
Without being able to recognize all kinds of R objects, the jQuery
trick to link R functions may be hard there (probably not terribly
hard...).

Regards,
Yihui
